items.stem: If the radius of the sphere is increased by 100%, then how much volume of the corresponding sphere is increased?
items.answer: Let r be the original radius, so the original volume is V = (4/3)πr³. Increasing the radius by 100% makes it 2r, and the new volume is (4/3)π(2r)³ = 8 × (4/3)πr³, i.e. 8 times the original. The new volume is therefore 800% of the original, so the increase is 800% − 100% = 700%.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 Delhi 2012

items.stem: A sphere is melted and half of the melted liquid is used to form 11 identical cubes, whereas the remaining half is used to form 7 identical smaller spheres. Find the ratio of the side of the cube to the radius of the new small sphere.
items.answer: Half the melted metal makes 11 cubes of side a and the other half makes 7 spheres of radius r, so the two halves are equal in volume: 11a³ = 7 × (4/3) × (22/7) × r³ = (88/3)r³. Hence a³ = (8/3)r³, so a/r = (8/3)^(1/3).
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 OD 2017

items.stem: Find the ratio of volumes of two cones with same radii.
items.answer: For two cones of equal radius r, V₁ : V₂ = (1/3)πr²h₁ : (1/3)πr²h₂. The common factor (1/3)πr² cancels, so the ratio of their volumes is h₁ : h₂.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board 2010

items.stem: The base radii of a cone and a cylinder are equal. If their curved surface areas are also equal, then what is the ratio of the slant height of the cone to the height of the cylinder?
items.answer: Equal curved surface areas over the same base radius r give πrl = 2πrh. Cancelling πr leaves l = 2h, so l : h = 2 : 1.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 Delhi 2013

items.stem: Find the ratio of lateral surface areas of two cylinders with equal height.
items.answer: For cylinders of equal height h and radii R and r, the lateral surface areas are 2πRh and 2πrh. Their ratio is 2πRh : 2πrh = R : r.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 Foreign 2016

items.stem: Find the ratio of volumes of two cylinders with equal height.
items.answer: For cylinders of equal height h and radii R and r, the volumes are πR²h and πr²h. Their ratio is πR²h : πr²h = R² : r².
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 Delhi 2014

items.stem: The diameter of a sphere is 6 cm. It is melted and drawn into a wire of diameter 2 mm. What is the length of the wire?
items.answer: The sphere has radius R = 3 cm, and the wire is a cylinder of radius r = 1 mm = 1/10 cm and length l. Melting conserves volume, so πr²l = (4/3)πR³, i.e. π × (1/10)² × l = (4/3)π × 3³. Then l/100 = 4 × 3² = 36, so l = 3600 cm = 36 m.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board 2009

items.stem: The diameter of hollow cone is equal to the diameter of a spherical ball. If the ball is placed at the base of the cone, what portion of the ball will be outside the cone?
items.answer: Although the base diameter of the cone equals the diameter of the ball, the cone tapers, so the ball cannot sink into it; the ball rests on the rim and only a small cap of it enters the cone. Hence more than 50% of the ball lies outside the cone.
items.concept: Solids in daily life are combinations
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board 2007

items.stem: If two solid hemispheres of same base radius r are joined together along their bases, then find the curved surface area of this new solid.
items.answer: Joining two solid hemispheres of radius r along their flat circular faces produces a solid sphere, and the two flat faces vanish inside the join. The curved surface area is 2πr² + 2πr² = 4πr².
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board 2010

items.stem: A solid piece of iron in the form of a cuboid of dimensions 49 cm × 33 cm × 24 cm, is moulded to form a solid sphere. What is the radius of the sphere?
items.answer: Moulding conserves volume, so (4/3)πr³ = 49 × 33 × 24 = 38808 cm³. Then 4 × (22/7)r³ = 38808 × 3, giving r³ = (38808 × 3 × 7)/(4 × 22) = 9261 = 21 × 21 × 21. Hence r = 21 cm.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board 2006

items.stem: Twelve solid spheres of the same size are made by melting a solid metallic cylinder of base diameter 2 cm and height 16 cm. What is the diameter of each sphere?
items.answer: The cylinder has radius 1 cm and height 16 cm, so its volume is π × 1² × 16 = 16π cm³. Twelve equal spheres of radius r have total volume 12 × (4/3)πr³ = 16πr³. Equating gives 16πr³ = 16π, so r³ = 1 and r = 1 cm. The diameter of each sphere is 2r = 2 cm.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 Delhi 201

items.stem: The total surface area of the given solid figure is .......... .
items.answer: The solid is a right circular cone standing on a cylinder of the same radius r. The surfaces that show are the flat base of the cylinder, the curved surface of the cylinder and the curved surface of the cone; the circle where the two meet is hidden. Total surface area = πr² + 2πrh + πrl = πr(r + 2h + l).
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board 2020 SQP Standard
items.ocr: Fill-in-the-blank item; the dimensions r, h and l are given only in the printed diagram, so the figure is required.

items.stem: A solid metallic cuboid 24 cm × 11 cm × 7 cm is melted and recast into solid cones of base radius 3.5 cm and height 6 cm. Find the number of cones so formed.
items.answer: Let n be the number of cones. Melting conserves volume, so n × (1/3) × (22/7) × (3.5)² × 6 = 24 × 11 × 7. The left side is 77n and the right side is 1848, so n = 1848/77 = 24. Thus 24 cones are formed.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 Foreign 2011

items.stem: The curved surface area of a cylinder is 264 m² and its volume is 924 m³. Find the ratio of its height to its diameter.
items.answer: Dividing the volume by the curved surface area, πr²h/(2πrh) = 924/264, so r/2 = 7/2 and r = 7 m. Substituting in 2πrh = 264 gives 2 × (22/7) × 7 × h = 264, so h = 6 m. Hence h : d = 6 : 14 = 3 : 7.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 2014

items.stem: A rectangular sheet paper 40 cm × 22 cm is rolled to form a hollow cylinder of height 40 cm. Find the radius of the cylinder.
items.answer: Rolling the sheet so that the 40 cm side becomes the height leaves the 22 cm side as the circumference of the base, so 2πr = 22. Then r = (22 × 7)/(2 × 22) = 7/2 = 3.5 cm.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 Foreign 2014

items.stem: A cylinder, a cone and a hemisphere have same base and same height. Find the ratio of their volumes.
items.answer: Equal base and equal height for a hemisphere force h = r. The volumes are then πr²h = πr³, (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)πr³ and (2/3)πr³, so the ratio is 1 : 1/3 : 2/3 = 3 : 1 : 2.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 Delhi 2014

items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 2012

items.stem: What is the ratio of the total surface area of the solid hemisphere to the square of its radius.
items.answer: The total surface area of a solid hemisphere is 2πr² for the curved part plus πr² for the flat circular face, i.e. 3πr². Dividing by r² gives 3π, so the required ratio is 3π : 1.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2, 2012

items.stem: The radius of sphere is r cm. It is divided into two equal parts. Find the whole surface of two parts.
items.answer: Cutting the sphere through its centre gives two hemispheres, and the cut exposes a new flat circular face on each. The whole surface of one part is 2πr² + πr² = 3πr², so for the two parts together it is 2 × 3πr² = 6πr².
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 2012

items.stem: The radii of two cylinders are in the ratio 2 : 3 and their heights are in the ratio 5 : 3, find the ratio of their volumes.
items.answer: V₁/V₂ = πr₁²h₁/(πr₂²h₂) = (r₁/r₂)² × (h₁/h₂) = (2/3)² × (5/3) = (4/9) × (5/3) = 20/27. The volumes are in the ratio 20 : 27.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 OD 2012

items.stem: If the radius of the base of a right circular cylinder is halved, keeping the height same, find the ratio of the volume of the reduced cylinder to that of original cylinder.
items.answer: The reduced cylinder has radius r/2 and the same height h, so its volume is π(r/2)²h = πr²h/4. Dividing by the original volume πr²h gives 1/4, so the ratio is 1 : 4.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 2012

items.stem: Volume of two spheres are in the ratio 64 : 27, find the ratio of their surface areas.
items.answer: From ((4/3)πr₁³)/((4/3)πr₂³) = 64/27 we get r₁³/r₂³ = 4³/3³, so r₁/r₂ = 4/3. The surface areas are in the ratio 4πr₁² : 4πr₂² = (r₁/r₂)² = (4/3)² = 16/9, that is 16 : 9.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 Delhi 2012

items.stem: Find the volume (in cm³) of the largest right circular cone that can be cut off from a cube of edge 4.2 cm.
items.answer: The largest such cone has height equal to the edge of the cube, 4.2 cm, and base radius equal to half the edge, 4.2/2 = 2.1 cm. Volume = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3) × (22/7) × (2.1)² × 4.2 = 19.4 cm³ (approximately).
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 OD 2012

items.stem: The circumference of the edge of a hemisphere bowl is 132 cm. When π is taken as 22/7, find the capacity of the bowl in cm³.
items.answer: The rim is a circle, so 2πr = 132 gives r = (132 × 7)/(2 × 22) = 21 cm. The capacity of the hemispherical bowl is (2/3)πr³ = (2/3) × (22/7) × 21 × 21 × 21 = 19404 cm³.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 2012

items.stem: Volume and surface area of a solid hemisphere are numerically equal. What is the diameter of hemisphere?
items.answer: Setting the two numbers equal, (2/3)πr³ = 3πr². Cancelling πr² gives (2/3)r = 3, so r = 9/2 units. The diameter is d = 2r = 9 units.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 Delhi 2017

items.stem: Three solid metallic spherical balls of radii 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm are melted into a single spherical ball, find its radius.
items.answer: Melting conserves volume, so (4/3)πr³ = (4/3)π(3³ + 4³ + 5³). Hence r³ = 27 + 64 + 125 = 216, and r = 6 cm.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2, 2014

items.stem: A solid sphere of radius r melted and recast into the shape of a solid cone of height r. Find the radius of the base of a cone.
items.answer: Let R be the base radius of the cone. Equating volumes, (4/3)πr³ = (1/3)πR² × r, so 4r³ = R²r and R² = 4r². Hence R = 2r.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 Delhi 2012

items.stem: Two cones have their heights in the ratio 1 : 3 and radii in the ratio 3 : 1. What is the ratio of their volumes?
items.answer: V₁/V₂ = ((1/3)πr₁²h₁)/((1/3)πr₂²h₂) = (r₁/r₂)² × (h₁/h₂) = (3/1)² × (1/3) = 9 × (1/3) = 3. The volumes are in the ratio 3 : 1.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board 2020 Delhi Standard

items.stem: A solid metallic cone of radius 2 cm and height 8 cm is melted into a sphere. Find the radius of sphere.
items.answer: Let R be the radius of the sphere. Equating volumes, (4/3)πR³ = (1/3)π × 2² × 8, so 4R³ = 32 and R³ = 8. Hence R = 2 cm.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 2014

items.stem: A glass cylinder with radius 10 cm has water to a height of 9 cm. A metal cube of 8 cm edge is immersed in it completely. Calculate the height by which water will rise in the cylinder. Use π = 22/7
items.answer: The cube is fully immersed, so the water it displaces equals its own volume. If h is the rise in level, π(10)²h = 8 × 8 × 8, so h = (8 × 8 × 8 × 7)/(22 × 10 × 10) = 3584/2200 = 1.629 cm (approximately).
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 2013
